name: robustness_m21_mismatchsince_cap_removed_mismatch
why: M21: the mismatchSince cap is removed, so a mismatch left over 25 days (link down) reads as new and the resync waits again.

edits.find: if (mismatchSince && elapsed(now, mismatchSince, STAMP_CAP_MS)) mismatchSince = (now - STAMP_CAP_MS) | 1;

name: robustness_m22_gate_s_between_hold
why: M22: the gate's between hold is written as now < betweenAt + hold. This is skipped only when the gate leaves a limit within BETWEEN_HOLD_MS (500 ms), or 3 s out of no_power, before the 2^32 wrap. A failing input supply there reads as a move, not no_power. SURVIVED: no wrap test cuts the gate's input supply in that window. Also not killed by test_system.cpp.

name: robustness_m7_inputs_are_configured_plain
why: M7: inputs are configured as plain INPUT (floating) instead of INPUT_PULLDOWN.

name: robustness_m8_in1_invert_becomes_remote
why: M8: in1_invert becomes remote-writable over LoRa (P_REMOTE), so polarity could be 'fixed' with invert from the house.

name: robustness_m9_acpower_also_counts_reading
why: M9: acPower() also counts a reading limit as AC present, so a dead IN3 opto no longer refuses commands while a limit reads.

name: robustness_m10_house_contact_sensor_reads
why: M10: the house contact sensor reads closed while the gate is between after leaving closed (holdingTravel), not only with the closed limit reading.

edits.replace: bool closed = gateState == GS_CLOSED || (holdingTravel(now) && lastEnd == GS_CLOSED);

name: robustness_m16_gate_refuses_commands_lost
why: M16: the gate refuses commands for lost AC only while its state is no_power. With a dead AC opto and a limit reading, it pulses.

name: robustness_m11_house_longer_holds_pending
why: M11: the house no longer holds its pending CMD (cmdHeld) when a new gate session HELLOs, so it resends after a gate restart that already pulsed.

name: robustness_m12_when_restarted_peer_s
why: M12: when the restarted peer's new session verifies, the held CMD is released and resent instead of dropped.

edits.replace: releaseCmd();  // resend it to the restarted peer

name: robustness_m13_house_opens_settle_window
why: M13: the house opens no settle window at boot.

name: robustness_m14_session_drawn_while_radio
why: M14: a session drawn while the radio was down (sessionWeak) is never redrawn once the radio answers, so a board whose radio failed at init never transmits and never links.

name: robustness_m23_gate_longer_sends_status
why: M23: the gate no longer sends a STATUS at once when a new house session appears, so a rebooted house waits for the next heartbeat.

name: robustness_m24_house_arms_first_status
why: M24: the house arms at the first STATUS instead of first STATUS + sync_window_ms. SURVIVED: masked by the 10 s boot settle window (ctrl_settle_ms) and by driveK1's window. In every restart test the first STATUS arrives within the settle window. Also not killed by test_system.cpp.

name: robustness_m25_housebegin_forgets_checksoon_after
why: M25: houseBegin forgets checkSoon, so after a house reboot an out-of-step controller is resynced only after mismatch_timeout_s, not as soon as the settle window closes.

name: robustness_m26_gate_reports_first_status
why: M26: the gate reports its first STATUS at once after boot instead of waiting for its inputs to settle (BOOT_SETTLE_MS). SURVIVED: no robustness test powers the opener down and up with the gate board (w.setGateRail). Gate restarts are board-only (gate.cut or reset), so the limits are always steady at boot. Also not killed by test_system.cpp.

name: robustness_m15_ctrlpowered_ignores_board_s
why: M15: ctrlPowered() ignores the board's VIN power good (ctrl_power_pmic). The controller relay dropping in a 12 V cut is then taken as the user's OFF.

name: robustness_m17_applyoutputs_drives_k1_target
why: M17: applyOutputs drives K1 to its target even during a resync, which cuts the resync pulse short: K1 is back 1 ms later, too short for the controller to see, so a controller out of step stays out of step.

name: robustness_m29_resync_window_ended_by_a_matching_edge
why: M29: a resync's window can be ended by an IN1 edge at the target level while K1 is still away (the user's edge in its debounce, or chatter): the controller then following K1 away is taken as the user, a command away from the gate.

name: robustness_m18_link_loss_contact_sensor
why: M18: on link loss the contact sensor no longer fails open (the linkloss_open check is dropped).

name: robustness_m27_when_controller_power_returns
why: M27: when controller power returns, the house opens a plain sync window instead of the ctrl_settle_ms settle window. (A first try that just deleted openSettleWindow failed the -Werror build with an unused parameter, so it doesn't count.) The chaos seeds did not catch it; the targeted tests did.

name: robustness_m28_opensyncwindow_may_now_shorten
why: M28: openSyncWindow may now shorten an open window, so a K1 change cuts the 10 s settle window to 3 s. SURVIVED: the simulated controller restores its level once at bootMs 1.5 s and never chatters. A restored level that matches the gate is suppressed, so nothing lands in the shortened part. Also not killed by test_system.cpp.

name: link_m1_busy_cap_not_restarted_by_a_clear_reading
why: clearToSend keeps busySince from an earlier busy reading after the channel reads clear, so the next busy reading forces a frame at once, into a neighbour's frame (found 2026-10-10 by link_stays_up_through_five_minutes_of_neighbour_traffic)

name: link_m2_backoff_not_capped
why: a frame held back past waitCapMs() still waits for its full backoff after the last frame heard, so frames heard more often than the backoff hold commands off until their TTL runs out

edits.replace: if (early && !(capped && quiet <= CAPPED_SLOT_MS && false)) return false;

name: link_m3_hold_counts_toward_the_wait_cap
why: a command held on a replayed HELLO keeps the channel wait it had begun, so once released it counts as held back past waitCapMs() and goes within a few ms of the frame that released it, skipping its backoff, logged lbt_forced (found on the bench, 0.13.7)

edits.find:
if (i == SLOT_CMD && cmdHeld) {  // the TTL keeps running
      s.lbt = {};
edits.replace: if (i == SLOT_CMD && cmdHeld) {  // the TTL keeps running

name: link_s1_house_takes_a_status_delivered_late
why: S1: the house takes any STATUS the link takes, also one older than the last it took (withheld at the house and played back late): an old closed sets it back to closed and closes the contact sensor while the gate stands open.

name: link_s2_house_link_kept_up_by_any_frame
why: S2: the house counts any frame from the gate as liveness, as before 0.13.9, so a STATUS withheld and played back late (or any withheld frame) keeps the link up, and the contact sensor from failing open, for another link timeout.

edits.find: uint32_t at = activeRole == ROLE_HOUSE ? houseStatusAt() : linkStats().lastRxAt;

name: link_s3_session_ids_from_the_rng_alone
why: S3: session ids are drawn from radioRandom32() alone again, not from the boot count (as before 0.13.9): a board whose entropy source is stuck comes back from a reboot or link restart with the same session and starting seq, and the peer drops its frames as replays.

name: fault_out_h1_hold_not_applied
why: H1: D5 drops as soon as a problem shows, fault_hold_s ignored: a brief blip (an AC flicker, a link dropout that recovers) trips the alarm.

name: fault_out_h2_recovery_waits_for_the_hold
why: H2: recovery waits out fault_hold_s too (a symmetric debounce), so D5 stays LOW for the hold after the problem is over, and after boot it rises only fault_hold_s after the board has decided.

name: fault_out_h3_healthy_at_boot
why: H3: D5 starts HIGH at boot (healthy until shown otherwise), so a reboot reads as healthy before anything is known, until the hold runs out.

name: fault_out_h4_starting_ignored
why: H4: the role's decision isn't waited for after boot: the house raises D5 as soon as the link is up (before it is armed), the gate as soon as it hears the house (before its inputs settled).

name: fault_out_h5_radio_ignored
why: H5: a radio that is down (faulted, failing to restart) isn't a problem: D5 stays HIGH until the link times out, if it ever does on that board.

name: fault_out_h6_link_ignored
why: H6: link loss isn't a problem: with the gate unheard the house keeps D5 HIGH, so the alarm never learns the gate went silent.

name: fault_out_h7_house_ignores_the_gate_ac_bit
why: H7: the house ignores the AC-lost bit (STATUS bit 6): the gate on its battery at a limit reads healthy at the house.

name: fault_out_h8_gate_ignores_its_ac
why: H8: the gate ignores its own AC power sense (IN3): no AC at the opener reads healthy at the gate.

name: fault_out_h9_no_power_ignored
why: H9: a gate reading no_power isn't a problem of its own: the health list and the log's bits leave it out (D5 still drops for the AC it implies).

name: fault_out_h10_fault_ignored
why: H10: a gate reading fault (both limits) isn't a problem: D5 stays HIGH on both boards while the gate's position can't be known.

name: fault_out_h11_driven_with_the_setting_off
why: H11: D5 is driven whatever fault_out says: an existing install, with fault_out off and D5 unwired or used otherwise, gets an output it never asked for.

name: fault_out_h12_house_relay_test_restarts_it
why: H12: the house's decision follows `armed` itself, which a K1 relay test clears for a while: the test reads as a new start, and with a short fault_hold_s D5 drops for it.

name: fault_out_h13_gate_decided_before_settling
why: H13: the gate counts as decided at once after boot, before its inputs settled and its first STATUS went out: a gate reboot raises D5 as soon as it hears the house.

edits.find: return !settling;  // settling ends with the first STATUS sent (gateLoop)

name: fault_out_h14_hold_not_wrap_safe
why: H14: the fault hold compares absolute times (now >= since + hold) instead of the signed elapsed(): a problem that starts within fault_hold_s before millis() wraps at 2^32 drops D5 at once.

name: fault_out_h15_gate_link_timeout_ignores_heartbeat
why: H15: the gate counts its link down after link_timeout_s alone, not 2.5 of its heartbeats: with a heartbeat_s past link_timeout_s / 2.5 (which the house allows, stretching its own timeout) the gate hears the house only once a heartbeat, so its link drops between heartbeats and D5 falls every cycle.

name: history_h1_bucket_written_during_a_pulse
why: H1: a completed history bucket is written to the flash (~0.5 s with the radio restart) while a relay pulses, so the pulse runs that much long

name: history_h2_clear_held_no_more
why: H2: hist.clear, which now writes the history log, isn't held while a relay pulses (blocksLoop)

name: history_h3_bad_crc_record_loaded
why: H3: the log takes a record without checking its CRC, so one torn by a power cut mid-write loads as the newest bucket (half of it erased bytes)

edits.find: if (get16(buf) != MAGIC || get32(buf + REC_LEN - 4) != crc32(buf, REC_LEN - 4)) return R_INVALID;

name: history_h4_torn_slot_written_over
why: H4: at boot the next record goes straight after the newest valid one, onto a slot a power cut tore, so it doesn't verify and that bucket is lost too (and the run ends there at the next boot)

name: history_h5_wrap_erases_the_newest_sector
why: H5: entering a sector, the log erases the one before it (the newest records) instead of the one it enters (the oldest)

edits.replace: if (head % PER_SECTOR == 0 && !extFlashEraseSector(slotAddr((head + SLOTS - 1) % SLOTS))) return false;

name: history_h6_newest_by_position
why: H6: the newest record is taken as the first valid one in slot order, not the one with the largest lseq: a boot then goes on from an old record (here the CLEARED one at the log's start)

name: history_h7_boot_loads_nothing
why: H7: the boot doesn't take the history the log holds: every reset starts it over at bucket 0

edits.replace: if (histLogBegin(HIST_DEPTH, takeBucket, p, next) && p == 0 && p >= 60

name: history_h8_clear_leaves_the_flash
why: H8: hist.clear empties the RAM only: the next reset brings the old history (and its period) back

name: history_h9_failed_write_retried_every_pass
why: H9: a bucket whose write failed is tried again on every loop pass, each one stopping the loop ~0.5 s and restarting the radio, so a failing chip takes the link down

name: history_h10_zeros_taken_for_a_garbled_bus
why: H10: a slot that reads zeros twice is taken for a garbled bus without asking the chip for its id: zeros the flash really holds (an erase cut short, another program's data) then turn the log off at every boot, for good, hist.clear included
